The Rivulated parrotfish (Scarus rivulatus) is a common herbivorous scarid inhabiting coral reefs and adjacent seagrass beds throughout the Indo-West Pacific. Newly hatched larvae are extremely small, with a wet weight at birth of approximately 0.00023 grams [Wwb = approximately 0.00023 grams], a value derived from the egg diameter of the butterflyfish genus Chaetodon used as a size proxy, reflecting the minute, pelagic eggs typical of broadcast-spawning reef fishes.

Juvenile Rivulated parrotfish grow steadily while grazing on algal turf on reef flats and adjoining seagrass meadows, an intermediate habitat use that distinguishes this species from more strictly reef-associated congeners. Individuals reach the total length at puberty of 10.3 centimeters [Lp = 10.3 centimeters], a value scaled from the relative body proportions of the related blue parrotfish Scarus coeruleus. At this size, the corresponding wet weight at puberty is approximately 19.5 grams [Wwp = approximately 19.5 grams].

Adults of this species ultimately attain a total length of 40 centimeters [Li = 40 centimeters], with a corresponding ultimate wet weight of approximately 1,254 grams [Wwi = approximately 1,254 grams]. This moderate adult body size supports the species' ecological role as a grazer that helps control algal overgrowth on reef substrates, contributing to the maintenance of coral-dominated reef states.

Reproductive output in the Rivulated parrotfish is exceptionally high, consistent with the broadcast-spawning strategy typical of scarids. At a water temperature of 28.5 °C [T = 28.5 °C], the maximum reproductive rate reaches approximately 3,288 eggs per day [Ri = approximately 3,288 eggs per day], reflecting the production of vast numbers of tiny, pelagic eggs that disperse widely on ocean currents. Longevity in this species reaches a maximum of approximately 20 years [am = approximately 20 years] at the same reference temperature, a considerable lifespan for a reef-associated scarid and one that allows individuals to contribute to reef herbivory and reproductive output across many successive spawning seasons at a temperature of 28.5 °C [T = 28.5 °C].
